name: Koalinth Caverns
summary: Sea-caves by the Cliffs of Moher where a Koalinth tribe from under the waves has made a fighting-hall, and keeps a line to home.

facts.text: The Koalinth are coastal hobgoblins; a tribe migrated from undersea homelands and took caves and old tunnels near the Cliffs of Moher, raids nearby settlements and can reach the sea to speak with its homeland. Why it left its element is unknown and 'hints at darker powers'. Level 20-30.

Its named include the Koalinth Castellan, the Koalinth Elder (a caster with crab escorts) and the Pelagian Alliant; Druid Tobryn of Tir Urphost gives the quest 'The Broken Seal' against the Castellan and Elder.
Region 223 holds Koalinth spectators, sentinels, guardians, warders, bouncers, envoys, wardens and wrestlers, Pelagian guards and crabs, and watery escorts.
Bot chat: 'koalinth caverns are wet, cold and full of fish people'.

The Koalinth Elder and the Koalinth Castellan each cast Inflict Suffering ('Target's attack speed reduced by 17%', 45 s, recast 7 s) and pull NPCs of their own package (KoalinthElderBaf, KoalinthCastellanBaf) within 1,500 into the fight; no spawn in the world data carries those packages.

The Broken Seal (Druid Tobryn): 'The koalinth would be better locked away, and I have found the magical means'; fetch a carved piece of aventurine from the Castellan and the glowing fungus from the Elder, return to Tobryn by the tree southwest of Tir Urphost, and use the medallion at the mouth of the cave.

Region 223 named spawns: Koalinth Elder (27), Koalinth Castellan (26), Pelagian Alliant (28), two Koalinth Diplomats (27-28), the Master of Ceremonies (22) and the Horned Cave Toad (23); also pelagian guards (31), cave toads and shock aqueous slugs.

Living Server lore: the koalinth came up the spring the mist lifted off Hy Brasil; the three accounts (fishermen, Diplomats, Tobryn); 'my arm has been to the koalinth'; the Elder's fungus light; the Alliant as the open sea's envoy; Tobryn's medallion as the seal.

Tier C named spawns of the Koalinth Caverns: two Koalinth Diplomats (27-28; one carries faction Koalinth, one none), Pelagian Alliant (28, faction Koalinth, a crab body like the pelagian guards and crabs round him), Koalinth Elder (27) and Koalinth Castellan (26) (KoalinthElder.cs, KoalinthCastellan.cs: Inflict Suffering, attack speed down 17% for 45 seconds; their call packages are carried by no spawn), Horned Cave Toad (23, among koalinth bouncers in the southern pools), Master of Ceremonies (22, in the fighting cave among spectators and bouncers).

story:
The Koalinth came up out of the sea, and the druids of Tir Urphost have never learned why. They are hobgoblins of the deep coast, cold and scaled and quick, and their true home lies somewhere under the waves off the Cliffs of Moher. One tribe of them left it. They took the sea-caves and the old tunnels behind the cliffs, raided the farmsteads above, and settled in as if they meant to stay. They have kept a door open to the sea. Their envoys go down it and come back up, and the druids would very much like to know what is said on the other side.

What is plain is that the tribe is a warrior people and the caves are a warrior's hall. There are wrestlers and bouncers, and there are spectators, and the spectators are not there by chance: the Koalinth hold fights in their great cave, as the old Hibernian kings held games, and watch them as keenly. Pelagian crabs scuttle under the benches. Wardens, warders and sentinels keep the doors. Somewhere deep in, the Elder speaks for the tribe and the Castellan holds its keep, and the druids suspect both of them answer to something further down.

Why would a sea-people leave the sea? Not for the farmland. The druids say it in a low voice: something drove them out, or something sent them up.

The fishermen of Tir Urphost date it exactly, in their way: the koalinth came up the same spring the mist lifted off Hy Brasil. That year the sea off the Cliffs of Moher ran cold in midsummer, the lobster pots came up empty and scoured, and the first koalinth were seen sitting on the black rocks below the cliffs at low tide, looking at the land the way a family looks at a house it has been told to move into. Within the month they had the sea-caves and the old smugglers' tunnels behind them.

There are three accounts of why, and each is told by someone with a reason. The fishermen say the koalinth were driven out: whatever woke under the western sea when the isle came out of the mist wanted their halls, and the cold water was its breath. The two Koalinth Diplomats, who will speak to a traveller if he speaks first, say their people came as envoys, to treat with the land, and that the trouble on the farms above is the work of the young and will stop when the land answers. Druid Tobryn of Tir Urphost, who has given more thought to it than anyone, writes that a people who come as envoys do not build a fighting-hall, and that the koalinth were sent.

Whoever is right, the tribe's order is plain to anyone who has been inside. The Elder speaks for the tribe from the deep eastern cave, by the light of a fungus that grows nowhere else on the coast. The Castellan holds the tribe's keep further north and carries a carved stone of aventurine that he will not put down. Neither is a great fighter. Both fight the koalinth way, which is to tire the arm before the blade has to do anything, and the Tir Urphost men say of a long day at the oars that their arm has been to the koalinth. Both still call into the deep caves when they are pressed, the way their people once called home through the sea-door, and nothing answers them any more. The Pelagian Alliant, the open sea's own envoy, keeps the northern landing with his guards and his crabs, an ally who has never said whose ally he is.

Near the mouth the Master of Ceremonies runs the fighting cave: the wrestlers and bouncers, the spectators who take sides, the watery escorts who bring each bout in. A horned toad bigger than the rest squats in the southern pools, and the koalinth feed it as a household feeds a dog.

Tobryn did not wait for an answer. With the Castellan's aventurine and the Elder's fungus he made a seal, and set it as a medallion at the mouth of the caves, to lock the koalinth away from the land they were sent to. The seal has been broken and set again more often than the druids admit. The sea-door is still open.
legend: Often empty and always cold. Good coin, poor loot until you reach the wrestling cave and the left branch. The Elder brings crab escorts; the Castellan is the druid's quest. Do not try to swim out through their sea-door, and do not cheer in the fighting cave: the spectators take sides. Twenties, cold and often empty. The Koalinth Elder (27, deep east) and the Koalinth Castellan (26, north) both cast Inflict Suffering, a 17% attack-speed debuff for 45 seconds, on whoever they fight: melee feels slow on them, so swap in casters or bring a haste. Both call for help, but in this world nothing is linked to them, so only what stands nearby comes. The Broken Seal from Druid Tobryn by the tree southwest of Tir Urphost: carved aventurine from the Castellan, glowing fungus from the Elder, back to Tobryn, then use the medallion at the mouth of the cave. Pelagian Alliant (28) with pelagian guards (31) in the north, two Koalinth Diplomats, the Master of Ceremonies (22) near the arena, the Horned Cave Toad (23) in the south. Shock slugs hit harder than they look.

loremaster.intro: The Koalinth Caverns, behind the Cliffs of Moher. A tribe of the sea's [hobgoblins] came up out of the waves and stayed. They keep a [door] to the sea, an [Elder] and a [Castellan], and the druids do not know [why] they came.

topics.hobgoblins: Cold, scaled and quick, a warrior people. Their great cave is a fighting hall with wrestlers and spectators.
topics.door: A way down to their home under the waves. Their envoys use it. What they say down there, we cannot hear.
topics.why: A sea-people does not leave the sea for farmland. Something drove them out, or something sent them up.
topics.Elder: The tribe's speaker, in the deep eastern cave by the light of a fungus that grows nowhere else on the coast. He calls into the deep when pressed. Nothing answers now. [Tobryn] wants his fungus.
topics.Castellan: Holds the tribe's keep in the north and carries a carved green stone of aventurine. He fights the koalinth way: tire the arm first. [Tobryn] wants his stone.
topics.Tobryn: Druid of Tir Urphost, who keeps by a tree southwest of the village. He made a [seal] from the Castellan's stone and the Elder's fungus to lock the koalinth away.
topics.seal: A medallion set at the mouth of the caves, of Tobryn's making. It has been broken and set again more often than the druids admit. The sea-door is still open.
topics.Alliant: The Pelagian Alliant, envoy of the open sea, keeps the northern landing with guards and crabs. Nobody knows whose ally he is.
topics.Koalinth Diplomat: There are two Koalinth Diplomats, and they will speak to a traveller if the traveller speaks first, which few do. They say their people came up the spring the isle rose as envoys, to treat with the land, and that the trouble on the farms above the cliffs is the work of the young of the tribe and will stop when the land answers. Druid Tobryn says the land has answered, with a seal. The diplomats say that was not an answer, it was a door being shut.
topics.Pelagian Alliant: The Pelagian Alliant is the envoy of the open sea, and keeps the northern landing of the caverns with his guards and his crabs, and the thing nobody tells the young before they go down is that the Alliant is a crab himself. He is an ally of the koalinth, the diplomats say. He has never said whose ally he is. The Tir Urphost fishers say the sea sends crabs ahead of everything it means to take back, the way a landlord sends a bailiff.
topics.Koalinth Elder: The Koalinth Elder is the tribe's speaker, in the deep eastern cave by the light of a fungus that grows nowhere else on the coast, with the koalinth guardians about him. He fights the koalinth way, the Tir Urphost fishers say: a touch of his and your arm has been to the koalinth, slow and heavy as if you had been swimming. When he is pressed he calls into the deep for help. Nothing answers now. Druid Tobryn wants his fungus for the seal.
topics.Koalinth Castellan: The Koalinth Castellan holds the tribe's keep in the north of the caverns, among the pelagian crabs, and carries a carved piece of green aventurine that Druid Tobryn wants for his seal. He fights as the Elder fights, tiring the arm first, so that the fighters who come against him feel they are swimming in their armour. He calls for his keep's garrison when he is pressed, and no garrison comes. The fishers say the keep was emptier than he admits long before anyone came.
topics.Horned Cave Toad: In the southern pools of the caverns, among the koalinth bouncers who keep order at the fighting cave, lives the Horned Cave Toad, a great horned thing the bouncers keep as the fighters' mascot. The wrestlers rub its horn for luck before a bout, the koalinth say, and the ones who lose say they rubbed it wrong. It is not fond of strangers, and the bouncers are less fond of strangers who bother it.
topics.Master of Ceremonies: The Master of Ceremonies runs the fighting cave near the mouth of the caverns: the wrestlers and the bouncers, the spectators who take sides, the watery escorts of living water who bring each fighter in. He calls the bouts, and the koalinth say he has never called one fairly, and that this is the point. A stranger who walks into the fighting cave is a bout, as far as he is concerned, and the spectators are already on their feet.

book.title: Druid Tobryn's Letter on the Koalinth
pages: To the Circle at Tir na Nog, from Tobryn at Tir Urphost. You asked what I have learned of the koalinth. Less than I would like. They are of the sea, unquestionably; their envoys go down through a flooded passage at the back of the caves and return some hours later, dry-eyed and in a hurry. Their Elder is no fool. Their Castellan is a soldier and nothing else. I have set the realm's young on both of them, with a seal of my making, to see who comes when the seal is broken.

Of the date. The fishermen are certain: the first koalinth sat on the rocks below the cliffs the spring the mist lifted off Hy Brasil. The sea ran cold that summer, and the pots came up scoured. I do not trust a coincidence that tidy, but I cannot disprove it either. If the isle's waking stirred something under the western sea, the koalinth may be refugees. Refugees do not usually arrive with a fighting-hall in mind. Nor do they leave the door behind them open. Theirs is open still, and cold air comes up it when the tide turns.

Of the fighting cave: yes, it is what you heard. They wrestle, and they watch, and they wager, I think, in shells. A Master of Ceremonies calls the bouts and escorts of living water bring each fighter in. It is very like a fair at Tara and I do not care for the likeness. A people who keep games are a people who mean to stay. A people from under the sea who mean to stay on land have been told the sea is no longer safe. I should like to know by whom, and what it was they were told.

Of the Elder and the Castellan, which is what the young ask me before they go. Neither is strong. Both wear a man down: the arm grows heavy in front of them, and stays heavy. Our fishermen say a long day at the oars has been to the koalinth. And both of them call, when they are hard pressed, into the deep caves, as their people once called home. I have listened at that door for a season. Nothing has ever called back. I find I am sorry for them, which I did not expect, and which I do not say in Tir Urphost.

Of the seal, last. The Castellan's carved aventurine and the Elder's fungus, worked into a medallion and set at the cave mouth, hold the tribe from the land for a while; a sea-people's own stone and their own light, turned against them. Every time it is broken, I make it again. I would rather know who sent them. Until I do, a lock on the door is the best a druid of Tir Urphost can offer the farms above. Send me the young, then. Every seal they carry out is a season's peace for someone.
